column2: The Transvaal Burghers Repudiate Crown Rule

The burghers have rejected the Crown administration and demand the restoration of their republic. Our officials withdraw from the local administration while preparations begin to reassert British authority. The dispute must now be settled between Britain and the restored South African Republic.

The assembled burghers proclaim the restoration of the South African Republic. The Crown administration gives way to the republican government, retaining the district offices and their records. With our independence declared, the commandos prepare to confront Britain.
The republic has resumed its government, but Britain refuses to abandon its claim to the Transvaal. The commandos are summoned to defend the restored republic. Victory will secure our independence

British Authority and the Transvaal Republic

The imperial administration and the Transvaal republic must be recorded as separate countries. Britain retains its overseas territories, while the burghers in the occupied Transvaal resume their demand for republican independence.
